instructions.primary_message: FOR THE ROAST CHICKEN: About 2 ½ hours before you plan to serve the chicken, set it on the counter and allow to come to room temperature for 30 minutes.
Once the chicken has come to room temperature, preheat oven to 375°F. Place oven rack in the lower position.
Small dice butter and place in a small bowl along with salt and pepper.
instructions.secondary_message:
4 tbsp butter, unsalted
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry thyme. Slide leaves off the stems and discard the stems. Add half to the bowl with the butter. (Set remaining thyme aside for the gravy.)
Wash, dry, and zest lemon into the bowl with the butter and set aside. Cut lemon into quarters and place in the bottom of a roasting pan.
Peel, halve, and roughly chop onion. Add to the roasting pan with the lemon.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels and add to the roasting pan, setting it on top of the lemon and onion, breast-side up.
Using the back of a spoon, mash and combine the herb butter.

Using your fingers, loosen and lift the skin away from the meat of the breasts. Stuff the openings with about 2/3 of the herb butter and press the skin to spread it out evenly over the meat. Spread and pat the remaining butter over the skin of the breast.
Season legs and thighs with salt and pepper.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Add water to the roasting pan.
Place chicken in the oven and roast until the skin starts to turn golden, about 40 minutes.

When the skin has started to turn golden, increase heat to 450°F. Continue to roast until the middle of a thigh or breast reaches 165°F, about 30 minutes more. When the chicken is done, remove from oven, transfer to a platter or cutting board, and let rest for 20 minutes.
FOR THE GRAVY: While the chicken is resting, carefully pour the drippings from the roasting pan into a medium bowl. Set aside to cool slightly.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the saucepan warms up, peel, halve, and mince additional onion.
Once the saucepan is hot, add butter and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
When the onion is soft, add flour and continue to cook, stirring often, until golden, 5-6 minutes more.
Meanwhile, use a spoon or ladle to skim off and discard any fat that has settled on top of the drippings. Pour drippings into a large measuring cup or jug and add broth, as needed, to measure 2 cups.
instructions.secondary_message: 12 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.primary_message: When the flour mixture is golden, slowly add the dripping-broth mixture, while whisking constantly. Add reserved fresh thyme, salt, and pepper; bring to a simmer, stirring occasionally. Once simmering, reduce heat to medium-low and cook until thickened, about 5 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: If you prefer a thinner gravy, add additional broth, a few tablespoons at a time, until desired consistency. Remove from heat.
instructions.secondary_message: 4 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.primary_message: Carve chicken and serve with gravy on the side.
